set.reason: Triangle sides are segments connecting vertices, so segment/end-point meanings occur in the definition.
set.scope: sides as line segments with endpoints

set.reason: The later target explicitly contains angle and side classification as a criterion. Acute/right/obtuse and equal-side recognition are necessary content components of that criterion; direct teaching removes the prior-lesson requirement but not the content.
set.scope: Classifying the triangle by its angles and identifying equal-side special cases

set.reason: The output is a reflected coordinate pair and plotted reflected figure; coordinate meaning is directly used.
set.scope: Writing and plotting symmetric point coordinates

set.reason: The theorem relates the sides of a right triangle; acute-angle complementarity is unnecessary. Root checked both endpoint-based reviews; each identifies the stated content or conditional method rather than a curriculum-order claim.
set.scope: Right-triangle, hypotenuse and leg meanings in the Pythagorean assertion

set.reason: Coordinate differences require the point-coordinate meaning, while slope is unnecessary. Root checked both endpoint-based reviews; each identifies the stated content or conditional method rather than a curriculum-order claim.
set.scope: Reading the coordinates of the two points whose distance is calculated
